title: Turkish & Islamic Arts Museum (İbrahim Paşa Palace): Hidden Sultanahmet Gem
seoTitle: Turkish & Islamic Arts Museum: İbrahim Paşa Palace (2026)
metaDescription: Inside Istanbul's Turkish & Islamic Arts Museum on the Hippodrome: Seljuk carpets, calligraphy, 2026 tickets, and MuseumPass rules.
quickAnswer: Sitting directly across the Hippodrome from the Blue Mosque inside the 16th-century İbrahim Paşa Palace, the Turkish & Islamic Arts Museum holds one of the world's finest collections of 13th-century Seljuk carpets, Islamic calligraphy, and Ottoman ethnography. Admission is €17 in 2026, covered by MuseumPass Istanbul, and a thorough visit takes 60 to 90 minutes with almost no queue.

body.text: Thousands of visitors photograph the Obelisk of Theodosius every day with their backs turned to the heavy stone facade of İbrahim Paşa Palace — never realizing it houses one of Türkiye's richest museum collections. If Sultanahmet's crowds leave you wanting quiet galleries and extraordinary craftsmanship, this is the single smartest stop to add. At [Itinerary of Türkiye](https://itineraryofturkiye.com/), our two founders routinely place it right after a morning Blue Mosque visit.
Why do most visitors walk right past one of Istanbul's finest museums on the Hippodrome?

Most travelers miss the Turkish & Islamic Arts Museum because its austere 16th-century stone facade looks like a closed historic wall rather than a museum entrance, and standard group tours rush straight between Hagia Sophia, the Blue Mosque, and Topkapı Palace.

Built for Pargalı İbrahim Paşa, Grand Vizier to Sultan Süleyman the Magnificent, the palace is one of the grandest surviving non-imperial Ottoman residences in Istanbul. Its entrance sits on the western edge of Sultanahmet Square at [At Meydanı Sokak No: 12](https://muze.gov.tr/Language/Index/EN?url=%2Fmuze-detay%3FsectionId%3DTIE01%26distId%3DTIE), just steps from the Serpent Column. Because it lacks aggressive street signage and stays off most half-day cruise excursions, you can walk in during peak season with virtually zero wait and step onto an elevated terrace overlooking the Hippodrome and the Blue Mosque's six minarets.
What rare Seljuk carpets, calligraphy and ethnographic halls sit inside?

Inside, chronological galleries span 1,300 years of Islamic art — anchored by rare 13th-century Anatolian Seljuk carpets, early Umayyad and Abbasid Quran manuscripts, Ottoman imperial tuğra calligraphy, and a lower-level ethnography wing recreating 19th-century Istanbul daily life.

According to the [Republic of Türkiye Ministry of Culture and Tourism](https://muze.gov.tr/Language/Index/EN?url=%2Fmuze-detay%3FsectionId%3DTIE01%26distId%3DTIE), the museum's carpet hall is regarded among the finest in the world, preserving large-format Seljuk wool rugs rescued from historic Konya and Beyşehir mosques alongside later Ushak and Ottoman court pieces. Moving through the vaulted upper halls, you encounter Damascene documents, inlaid metalwork, carved wood minbars, Iznik ceramics, and a Holy Relics section. Downstairs off the courtyard, the ethnography galleries shift focus to everyday Anatolian and Ottoman life — displaying nomadic Yörük black tents, woven kilims, traditional looms, and reconstructed 19th-century Istanbul living rooms.

body.text: Yes — [MuseumPass Istanbul](https://muze.gov.tr/urun-detay?CatalogNo=WEB-MSP01-05-009) (€105 for 5 consecutive days in 2026) covers daytime entry to the Turkish & Islamic Arts Museum, while standalone foreign-visitor e-tickets cost €17. Note that MuseumPass is not valid for after-hours night museum programs past 19:00.

As listed on the official [Ministry of Culture and Tourism ticketing portal](https://www.muze.gov.tr/Language/Index/EN?url=%2Furun-ekle%3FcatalogNo%3DWEB-MLT01-01-009), the €17 individual ticket is charged in Turkish Lira at the previous business day's Central Bank exchange rate. The museum opens daily from 09:00 to 18:30, with last MuseumPass entry recorded at 18:45 during extended summer schedules (verify seasonal cutoffs on the day of your visit).
How long does a visit take?

Plan 60 to 90 minutes for a balanced walk through the upper art galleries, the carpet hall, and the downstairs ethnography wing — or up to two hours if you read every manuscript label and linger in the courtyard cafe.

Because the galleries flow in a clear, chronological loop around İbrahim Paşa Palace's stone courtyard, the museum never feels exhausting after a morning on your feet. It pairs naturally with a Blue Mosque prayer-time closure: when the mosque closes for noon (Dhuhr) prayer, cross the Hippodrome, spend an unhurried hour inside the museum, and step back out once the square clears.

items: Find the entrance at Binbirdirek, At Meydanı Caddesi No: 12, directly opposite the Blue Mosque.
Bring your MuseumPass Istanbul (valid for daytime entry) or purchase a €17 single ticket at the desk or on muze.gov.tr.
Start upstairs in the chronological Islamic art and Seljuk carpet halls before descending to the courtyard ethnography wing.
Pause on the palace's upper stone terrace for an elevated photo of the Hippodrome and Blue Mosque.
Pair the visit with a midday Blue Mosque prayer closure to skip crowds at both sites.

faq.q: Is the Turkish & Islamic Arts Museum open every day?
faq.a: Yes, it operates daily from 09:00 to 18:30 (with occasional adjustments on the first morning of religious holidays). Check muze.gov.tr for seasonal updates.

faq.q: How much is the Turkish & Islamic Arts Museum ticket in 2026?
faq.a: Standalone admission for foreign visitors is €17 (paid in equivalent Turkish Lira), and daytime entry is included with MuseumPass Istanbul (€105).

faq.q: Is it worth visiting if I am already going to Topkapı Palace?
faq.a: Yes. Topkapı showcases imperial Ottoman court life and architecture, whereas this museum specializes in pan-Islamic manuscripts, world-class 13th-century Seljuk carpets, and Anatolian ethnography you will not see at Topkapı.

faq.q: Can you take photos inside the museum?
faq.a: Non-flash photography is permitted in most galleries. Flash is strictly prohibited to protect fragile ancient carpets, parchment manuscripts, and historic textiles.

faq.q: Is the museum suitable for children or families?
faq.a: Yes. The compact 60-to-90-minute layout, nomadic tents, and reconstructed 19th-century Istanbul rooms in the ethnography section hold younger visitors' attention well.

faq.q: Where is the nearest tram stop?
faq.a: Take the T1 Kabataş–Bağcılar tram to the Sultanahmet stop; the palace entrance on the Hippodrome is a flat four-minute walk south.
